question: What happened to earnings per share and the share count, and are buybacks shrinking it?

answer.summary: Diluted EPS rose to $6.13 in FY2023, up 0.3% YoY from $6.11 in FY2022 [F00055], after a stronger 8.9% gain in FY2022 [F00056]. The share count continued to shrink: diluted weighted-average shares fell 3.1% YoY to 15,812,547,000 in FY2023 [F00061], following a 3.2% decline in FY2022 [F00062]. Buybacks did slow materially — repurchases of common stock dropped 13.3% YoY to $77.55B in FY2023 [F00251], down from $89.40B in FY2022 [F00252] and $85.97B in FY2021 [F00253]. Despite the slower buyback pace, the share count still declined, so buybacks continued to shrink the denominator, just at a reduced rate. Dividends kept growing (+1.2% YoY to $15.03B) [F00248], so total shareholder returns fell 11.2% YoY to $92.58B in FY2023 [F01448].

key_numbers.metric: Payments for repurchase of common stock

drivers: Share count reduction (buybacks) is the primary driver of EPS growth: diluted shares declined 3.1% in FY2023 [F00061] while EPS rose 0.3% [F00055].
Buyback pace decelerated: repurchases fell 13.3% YoY in FY2023 to $77.55B [F00251], the largest single drag on total shareholder returns.
Dividends offset part of the buyback decline, growing 1.2% YoY to $15.03B [F00248], but not enough to prevent total returns from falling 11.2% YoY [F01448].
risks_and_red_flags: Buyback activity is shrinking: repurchases down 13.3% YoY in FY2023 [F00251], and total shareholder returns down 11.2% YoY [F01448], which could slow future EPS accretion.
EPS growth nearly stalled in FY2023 at +0.3% [F00055], coincides with the buyback slowdown.
Approximately 24 million RSUs were excluded from diluted EPS in FY2023 as antidilutive [T00460], meaning reported diluted EPS understates potential dilution if those shares were included.
